author: yaron-e92
body:
This pull request introduces a new "cut-in-line" priority feature for tasks, allowing users to mark tasks to be selected ahead of others either once or until completion. The implementation includes changes across the domain model, persistence, business logic, and user interface to support setting, persisting, and displaying cut-in-line priorities.

**Cut-in-line priority feature:**

* Added a new enum `CutInLineMode` with `None`, `Once`, and `UntilCompletion` options to represent cut-in-line priority states for tasks. (`ShuffleTask.Domain/Enums.cs` [ShuffleTask.Domain/Enums.csR38-R44](diffhunk://#diff-cd395f21aeba2ed989d29894ceea3fc73e0cb21ee9af1285dbf938ba48dad7b3R38-R44))
* Extended the `TaskItemData` model and related copy/serialization logic to include the new `CutInLineMode` property. (`ShuffleTask.Domain/TaskItemData.cs` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-76ccd231e89c330bf9d55c4ba03b27b8ab659fc7b00b2870a33d0c541765c397R39-R40) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-76ccd231e89c330bf9d55c4ba03b27b8ab659fc7b00b2870a33d0c541765c397R62)
* Updated the database schema and storage logic to persist the `CutInLineMode` property for tasks. (`ShuffleTask.Persistence/StorageService.cs` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b26f218a46958d05e581ef67016e638030817b932b4bba83852a76540fe5a6f1R81) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b26f218a46958d05e581ef67016e638030817b932b4bba83852a76540fe5a6f1R167)
* Modified the task selection logic in the scheduler to prioritize and immediately select tasks with a non-`None` cut-in-line mode. (`ShuffleTask.Application/Services/SchedulerService.cs` [ShuffleTask.Application/Services/SchedulerService.csR62-R71](diffhunk://#diff-f17623ab52d9533559ea74ff5486d5e25af1c72baef6f515289771c490ef6e95R62-R71))
* Ensured that "Once" cut-in-line mode is cleared after use, and "UntilCompletion" is cleared when the task is completed. (`ShuffleTask.Presentation/Services/ShuffleCoordinatorService.cs` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-1b24caf0b7c669e453c0b3993649c2a9b9ddc669f9caa12afc04473df0549cfdR407) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-1b24caf0b7c669e453c0b3993649c2a9b9ddc669f9caa12afc04473df0549cfdR464-R474)

**User interface and interaction:**

* Added UI controls to the task edit page for setting the cut-in-line mode, and updated view models to support this property. (`ShuffleTask.Presentation/ViewModels/EditTaskViewModel.cs` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-11fb5331e34faa905828bd374835bf55bfd27abebdae92a95d3f05a9cc6805f0R74-R76) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-11fb5331e34faa905828bd374835bf55bfd27abebdae92a95d3f05a9cc6805f0R96-R97) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-11fb5331e34faa905828bd374835bf55bfd27abebdae92a95d3f05a9cc6805f0R176) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-11fb5331e34faa905828bd374835bf55bfd27abebdae92a95d3f05a9cc6805f0R222); `ShuffleTask.Presentation/Views/EditTaskPage.xaml` [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-1e23beb786ec4f8fbbf1ade8bcd49a994118b91799cbc5015a130ada5ba95effR26) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-1e23beb786ec4f8fbbf1ade8bcd49a994118b91799cbc5015a130ada5ba95effR164-R174) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-1e23beb786ec4f8fbbf1ade8bcd49a994118b91799cbc5015a130ada5ba95effL171-R183) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-1e23beb786ec4f8fbbf1ade8bcd49a994118b91799cbc5015a130ada5ba95effL182-R194)
* Implemented new swipe actions on the task list for quickly setting or clearing cut-in-line priority for tasks. (`ShuffleTask.Presentation/Views/TasksPage.xaml` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d128bcb5f0c2620c003291d921685e99aefff8c24ee2b850f157d787feb784acR53-R64) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d128bcb5f0c2620c003291d921685e99aefff8c24ee2b850f157d787feb784acL73-R101); `ShuffleTask.Presentation/Views/TasksPage.xaml.cs` [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-d081a47981cff1ef7d78550f5a9d30695f23476dd0dbf924a4cd750c9f37f2dfR67-R90)
* Updated the task list UI to display a badge indicating when a task has cut-in-line priority, including color and text variations for each mode. (`ShuffleTask.Presentation/ViewModels/TasksViewModel.cs` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-11472fdeac4a3d2ddc9dcc0d8c3a38fc9a1a38f708d55737e0e313de54f129c5R65-R80) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-11472fdeac4a3d2ddc9dcc0d8c3a38fc9a1a38f708d55737e0e313de54f129c5R132-R154); `ShuffleTask.Presentation/Views/TasksPage.xaml` [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-d128bcb5f0c2620c003291d921685e99aefff8c24ee2b850f157d787feb784acL73-R101)

**Persistence and preferences:**

* Added a preference key for tracking the cut-in-line task ID. (`ShuffleTask.Presentation/PreferenceKeys.cs` [ShuffleTask.Presentation/PreferenceKeys.csR11](diffhunk://#diff-e0c395e1ea045b5a60d1b67b7751ea2edad9122a5d96bde375cc91d232a44f8dR11))

**Testing:**

* Updated domain tests to cover the new `CutInLineMode` property in task data and equality assertions. (`ShuffleTask.Tests/Domain/TaskItemTests.cs` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-40df98f60d6e657b39579a5e48858d7ef69d2cb7994b5af1c05c56fb6d6d552aL105-R106) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-40df98f60d6e657b39579a5e48858d7ef69d2cb7994b5af1c05c56fb6d6d552aR131)

This PR introduces a new function to create and insert signature fields into PDF documents, modernizes image handling, and updates dependencies to keep the codebase current. These changes improve the flexibility, maintainability, and future compatibility of the project.

### Features
Add function to create and insert easily signature fields in PDFs. (available trough the feature "signature-fields", Fixes #6) 
### Refactor
Switch image handling to use BufRead and Seek traits for better flexibility
Enhance error handling for PDF signature processing
### Maintenance
Update dependencies to latest versions
Bump version to match new changes

Verified PDF signature fields are created and displayed correctly.
Checked image processing on multiple PDF files to ensure backward compatibility.
Build passes and dependencies resolve without conflicts.

Procedure declarations are sent as `SymbolKind::CONSTRUCTOR`, matching the context used in syntax highlighting.

body:
fix: Corrige integração da agenda e melhora organização de rotas

Esta branch contém correções críticas e melhorias de organização para resolver problemas de integração da agenda e garantir que todos os filtros de sessões funcionem corretamente.

## 🐛 Correções Críticas

1.  **Session Model - Associação Sequelize**
    - **Arquivo:** `models/Session.js`
    - **Problema:** `EagerLoadingError` devido a um *alias mismatch* na associação.
    - **Solução:** Adicionado `as: 'cliente'` na associação `Session.belongsTo(client)`.
    - **Impacto:** Resolve o erro 500 que ocorria ao buscar sessões com os dados do cliente incluídos.

2.  **Client Service - Sintaxe Import/Export**
    - **Arquivo:** `services/clientService.js`
    - **Problema:** Uso incorreto de `import` (ES6) em um projeto configurado para CommonJS.
    - **Solução:** A sintaxe foi convertida para `const { Op, fn, col, where } = require('sequelize')`.
    - **Impacto:** Remove o erro de sintaxe que impedia a execução do serviço.

3.  **Session Controller - Query Parameters**
    - **Arquivo:** `controllers/sessionController.js`
    - **Problema:** O código estava tentando acessar `req.date` em vez do parâmetro correto `req.query.date`.
    - **Solução:** Todas as funções `ByDate` foram corrigidas para extrair a data de `req.query`.
    - **Impacto:** Garante que os filtros por data funcionem como esperado.

## 🗂️ Melhorias de Organização

4.  **Session Routes - Reestruturação**
    - **Arquivo:** `routes/sessionRoutes.js`
    - **Melhoria:** As rotas `GET` foram agrupadas no início do arquivo para melhorar a clareza e a manutenção.
    - **Rotas reorganizadas:**
        - `/pendentes` - Sessões pendentes
        - `/realizadas` - Sessões realizadas
        - `/canceladas` - Sessões canceladas
        - `/cliente/:clienteId/*` - Filtros por cliente específico
    - **Impacto:** O código das rotas está mais legível, organizado e fácil de manter.

## Problem

The "get in touch" button (`.btn-secondary`) had a problematic hover effect in dark mode that included:
- Aggressive yellow/golden color change that looked out of place
- Sweeping gradient animation from pseudo-elements creating visual artifacts
- A perceived "slant to the left" caused by uncontained pseudo-elements and scale transform

## Solution

Simplified the `.btn-secondary` hover effect by:
- Removing the `::before` and `::after` pseudo-elements that created the distracting gradient sweep animations
- Adding `position: relative` and `overflow: hidden` to properly contain button effects
- Replacing the yellow accent color hover with a subtle background color change using theme variables
- Removing the `scale(1.02)` transform that contributed to the visual distortion
- Reducing shadow intensity for a cleaner, more professional appearance

## Changes

- **Removed**: 28 lines of aggressive pseudo-element styling
- **Added**: 2 lines for proper containment (`position: relative`, `overflow: hidden`)
- **Updated**: Hover state to use subtle, theme-consistent colors and effects

## Result

The button now has a clean, professional hover effect that works well in both dark and light modes without any visual artifacts or aggressive animations.

body:
## Overview
Refactored the `/api/hello` endpoint to follow the Model-View-Controller (MVC) pattern, moving from minimal API approach to a controller-based architecture with proper dependency injection.

## Changes

### Architecture
- **Controllers**: Created `HelloController` in the `Controllers` folder to handle `/api/hello` requests
- **Services**: Created `DummyService` in the `Services` folder to provide business logic
- **Dependency Injection**: Registered `DummyService` with ASP.NET Core's built-in DI container

### Implementation Details

**HelloController** (`Controllers/HelloController.cs`):
- Inherits from `ControllerBase` following ASP.NET Core best practices
- Uses attribute routing `[Route("api/[controller]")]` which maps to `/api/hello`
- Receives `DummyService` via constructor injection
- Returns the same response format as before: `{"message":"Hello from the API!"}`

**DummyService** (`Services/DummyService.cs`):
- Encapsulates the message generation logic
- Registered as a scoped service in the DI container
- Provides a clean separation of concerns

**Program.cs**:
- Added `builder.Services.AddControllers()` to enable MVC controllers
- Registered `DummyService` using `builder.Services.AddScoped<DummyService>()`
- Replaced the minimal API endpoint with `app.MapControllers()`
- Left `/weatherforecast` endpoint unchanged as required

### Benefits
- Better code organization following SOLID principles
- Improved testability through dependency injection
- Scalable architecture for future endpoint additions
- Maintains backward compatibility - `/api/hello` returns the same response

### Testing
✅ Project builds successfully  
✅ `/api/hello` endpoint returns `{"message":"Hello from the API!"}`  
✅ `/weatherforecast` endpoint continues to work (unchanged)  
✅ Dependency injection properly wires up `DummyService` to `HelloController`

## Overview This PR addresses issue #7 by improving the checkout page layout and implementing payment confirmation flows to prevent cart modifications during checkout. ## Changes Made ### 1. Compact Product Cards with Grid Layout Product cards in the "Itens do Pedido" section are reorganized using CSS Grid for a more compact layout while preserving all information: - **Layout**: Changed from flex to CSS Grid with emoji, details, and controls in a single row - **Card padding**: `1.5rem` → `0.75rem` - **Gaps**: Reduced from `1.5rem` to `0.5-1rem` between elements - **Description**: Truncated to 1 line instead of 2 for space efficiency - **Controls**: Quantity buttons and remove button more compact (28px buttons, reduced spacing) - **Emoji**: Kept at original 3rem size, positioned as grid item - **Subtotal**: Moved to second row spanning details and actions columns ### 2. Scrollable Items List Added scrollbar functionality to prevent infinite list growth: - **Scrollable container**: Items wrapped in `.checkout-items-list` div with `max-height: calc(100vh - 200px)` - **Custom scrollbar**: 8px width styled with purple theme matching the site colors - **Fixed elements**: Title "Itens do Pedido" and "Total do Pedido" remain visible during scroll - **Responsive**: Adjusts to viewport height automatically ### 3. Payment Completion Flow Modified payment completion to keep users on the checkout page: - **After payment confirmation**: Cart is cleared and all payment state is reset - **User stays on checkout page**: Shows "Seu carrinho está vazio!" message instead of redirecting to home - **Ready for new order**: User can immediately add more items without navigation ### 4. Payment Locking and Confirmation Modals Implemented a robust payment flow that prevents cart modifications during checkout: **WhatsApp Payment:** 1. User clicks WhatsApp button → WhatsApp opens in new tab 2. All cart controls (quantity +/-, remove buttons) are disabled 3. Payment method buttons are disabled 4. Confirmation modal appears: "Você finalizou a compra via WhatsApp?" 5. If confirmed: cart is cleared, user stays on checkout page 6. If cancelled: all controls re-enabled, cart remains intact **PIX Payment:** 1. User clicks PIX button → PIX form displayed 2. All cart controls disabled during form entry and QR code display 3. After QR code generation, confirmation modal appears: "Você concluiu o pagamento via PIX?" 4. If confirmed: cart is cleared, user stays on checkout page 5. If cancelled via "Voltar" button or modal: controls re-enabled, form hidden, cart remains intact **Technical Implementation:** - Added `isProcessingPayment` state to track payment status - Added `showConfirmationModal` state for modal display - Modified all cart action handlers to check `isProcessingPayment` before executing - Implemented `handlePaymentConfirmation()` to handle modal responses and stay on checkout page - Added CSS for modal overlay, content box, and disabled button states - Added CSS Grid layout for compact card reorganization - Added scrollable container with custom scrollbar styling - Fixed phone validation to allow email-only submissions (validates phone only if user enters > 2 digits) ## Why These Changes Matter **Before:** - Users could accidentally delete items from their cart while in the middle of a PIX payment, causing the entire checkout form to disappear - Items list would grow infinitely requiring excessive scrolling - Font sizes were reduced making content harder to read **After:** - The checkout process is locked during payment, preventing accidental modifications - Items list has a scrollbar when it grows beyond viewport, keeping title and total visible - Layout is reorganized with Grid for compactness while maintaining original font sizes for readability - Users stay on checkout page after payment completion, ready to place another order ## Testing - ✅ All changes build successfully - ✅ Grid layout displays correctly with all items - ✅ Scrollbar appears and functions properly with 6+ items - ✅ Title and total remain visible during scroll - ✅ WhatsApp flow: confirmation modal → completed → cart cleared, stays on checkout - ✅ WhatsApp flow: confirmation modal → cancelled → cart intact - ✅ PIX flow: form → QR code → modal → completed → cart cleared, stays on checkout - ✅ PIX flow: form → back button → cart intact - ✅ PIX flow: form → QR code → modal → cancelled → cart intact - ✅ Email-only validation works correctly - ✅ All cart controls properly locked/unlocked during payment states Closes #7

body:
- [x] Fix Contact section field formatting (completed in previous commits)
- [x] Create user story for Contact template configuration
- [x] Implement config UI as template string editor
- [x] Update ContactSectionOperations to use template renderer
- [x] Add hyphen suffix for newline suppression
- [x] Make hyphen suppression unconditional (not dependent on content)
- [x] Fix newline suppression implementation to actually work
- [x] Fix hyphen whitespace control - trim and normalize
- [x] Add ## Contact heading to default template
- [x] Ensure build produces no errors
- [x] Update all tests and documentation

## Fixed Hyphen Whitespace Control

The hyphen suffix wasn't working correctly because it only removed the trailing newline after the closing tag, but didn't handle the leading/trailing whitespace within the section content itself.

### Issue
With template:
```
## Contact
{{#EMAIL-}}
- 📧 {{#FIRST}}{{LABEL}} {{VALUE}}{{/FIRST}}
{{/EMAIL-}}
{{#TEL-}}
- 📞 {{#FIRST}}{{LABEL}} {{VALUE}}{{/FIRST}}
{{/TEL-}}
```

Was producing:
```
## Contact

- 📧 Home name@example.com

- 📞 Work (555) 555-5555

```

Extra blank lines appeared because the section content included `\n- 📧...\n`, and we were only suppressing the newline after `{{/EMAIL-}}`, not the ones inside the section.

### Solution
When hyphen suffix is present:
1. **Trim leading/trailing whitespace** from section content using `.trim()`
2. **Add exactly one newline** after the section (for separation from next section)
3. For empty sections, produce **no output at all**

Now produces:
```
## Contact
- 📧 Home name@example.com
- 📞 Work (555) 555-5555
```

### Implementation
```typescript
if (hyphen === '-') {
  result = result.trim();
  // Add a newline after the trimmed content
  return result + '\n';
} else {
  // Preserve original behavior
  return result + trailingNewline;
}
```

### Benefits
✅ **Clean output** - No extra blank lines  
✅ **Predictable** - Trim whitespace, add single newline  
✅ **Flexible** - Template can have readable formatting without affecting output  
✅ **Compact** - Produces tight, professional-looking contact sections

### Documentation Updated
- `docs/contact-template-syntax.md` - Rewrote whitespace control section with correct behavior
- `docs/user-stories.md` - Updated whitespace control explanation
- Settings UI - Changed to "trim whitespace and add single newline"

### Tests
✅ All 27 contact section tests passing  
✅ Build succeeds with no errors

author: austinbjohnson
body:
## Summary

Phase 1 of architectural refactoring: Extract infrastructure components from SonosController god object into focused, testable modules.

## What Changed

### New Infrastructure Components (623 lines)
- **SSDPSocket** (90 lines): Low-level BSD socket wrapper for SSDP discovery
- **SSDPDiscoveryService** (180 lines): SSDP device discovery protocol with actor isolation
- **SonosNetworkClient** (208 lines): Type-safe SOAP/UPnP communication layer
- **XMLParsingHelpers** (145 lines): Centralized XML parsing utilities

### Refactored SonosController
- Integrated all new infrastructure components
- Removed manual URLRequest construction throughout
- Replaced inline XML parsing with helpers
- **Result**: 1,732 → 1,471 lines (**-261 lines, -15%**)

## Benefits

✅ **Separation of Concerns**: Infrastructure, networking, and parsing now isolated  
✅ **Type Safety**: SOAPRequest struct eliminates string-based SOAP construction  
✅ **Testability**: Each component can be unit tested independently  
✅ **Maintainability**: Clear boundaries between responsibilities  
✅ **Concurrency Safety**: Proper actor isolation and @Sendable closures  
✅ **No Behavior Changes**: All functionality works exactly as before

## Architecture

```
Infrastructure/
├── SSDPSocket.swift              # BSD socket wrapper
├── SSDPDiscoveryService.swift    # Device discovery
├── SonosNetworkClient.swift      # SOAP/UPnP client
└── XMLParsingHelpers.swift       # Parsing utilities

SonosController.swift             # Now uses infrastructure
```

## Testing

Tested successfully:
- ✅ Device discovery via SSDP
- ✅ Volume control (individual and group)
- ✅ Group topology detection
- ✅ All existing functionality intact

## Next Steps

This is Phase 1 of the god object refactoring. Future phases will:
- Extract domain layer (repositories, managers, coordinator)
- Refactor MenuBarContentView with MVVM pattern
- Implement dependency injection
- Add comprehensive tests

## Related

- Addresses P1 Architecture task in ROADMAP.md:61 (SonosController god object)
- Follows architecture plan from architecture-advisor agent

body:
## Summary

Implements non-blocking file uploads using S3 presigned URLs and reconfigures workers for Kubernetes horizontal pod autoscaling.

## Changes

### Non-blocking Upload System
- Frontend: New `uploadConversationChunkWithPresignedUrl` function
- Backend: Endpoints for presigned URL generation and upload confirmation
- API server no longer handles file transfers
- Direct client to S3 uploads
- Retry logic: 3 attempts with exponential backoff
- Rate limiting: 10 requests/min per conversation
- Progress tracking through upload stages

### Worker Configuration
- API: Switched from uvicorn to gunicorn (2 workers/pod)
- Network workers: 3×50 → 2×20 threads per pod
- CPU workers: 4×6 → 2×4 threads per pod
- All settings configurable via environment variables:
  - `API_WORKERS=2`
  - `NETWORK_WORKER_PROCESSES=2`, `THREADS=20`
  - `CPU_WORKER_PROCESSES=2`, `THREADS=4`

### Other
- Fixed DIRECTUS_PUBLIC_URL handling for absolute/relative URLs
- Added dependencies: gunicorn, trankit, torch
- Updated vite proxy to localhost:8001

## Files Changed

**Backend:**
- `dembrane/api/participant.py`: Presigned URL endpoints
- `dembrane/s3.py`: URL generation logic
- `dembrane/service/conversation.py`: Chunk handling updates
- `prod*.sh`: Worker configuration scripts
- `pyproject.toml`: Dependencies

**Frontend:**
- `lib/api.ts`: Upload implementation
- `config.ts`: URL handling
- `vite.config.ts`: Proxy config

## Notes

- No breaking changes to existing upload functionality
- Worker settings now environment-configurable
- Risk: LOW, easy rollback

---

**Commits:**
- feat: optimize workers for Kubernetes horizontal scaling
- Update configuration and dependencies

  * Chunk creation now records file URLs consistently; safer URL logging and stricter filename/key validation to prevent path traversal; clearer upload/confirmation error handling.

* **Chores**

author: copilot
body:
## Overview
Implemented a complete web-based dice roller application using Node.js and Express, providing an interactive interface for rolling multiple dice with various numbers of sides.

## Implementation Details

### Backend (Node.js + Express)
- Created an Express server that serves static files and provides a REST API endpoint
- Implemented `/api/roll` POST endpoint that accepts dice configuration and returns randomized results
- Added input validation to ensure sides are between 2-100 and dice count is between 1-10
- Server runs on port 3000 by default (configurable via PORT environment variable)

### Frontend
- Built a clean, modern web interface with gradient purple styling
- Supports rolling 1-10 dice simultaneously
- Provides dropdown selection for common dice types: D4, D6, D8, D10, D12, D20, and D100
- Displays individual dice results with animated roll effects
- Calculates and displays the total sum of all dice rolled
- Fully responsive design that works on desktop and mobile devices

### API Usage
The REST API can be used programmatically:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/roll \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"sides": 20, "count": 3}'
```

Response:
```json
{
  "rolls": [17, 14, 19],
  "sum": 50,
  "sides": 20,
  "count": 3
}
```

## Getting Started

1. Install dependencies:
```bash
npm install
```

2. Start the server:
```bash
npm start
```

3. Open browser to http://localhost:3000

## Screenshots

**Initial Interface:**
![Dice Roller Interface](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/050a8883-876a-40fb-ad12-b10414af991a)

**Single Die Roll Result:**
![Single Die Roll](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2ebbb131-e6dc-48e6-a046-5e1ac064437d)

**Multiple Dice (5 D6) with Total:**
![Multiple D6 Dice](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0084fa37-5b4b-44f9-8e1c-dc37d089145c)

**D20 Dice Roll:**
![D20 Roll](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/68a2029c-9bc7-484a-85da-2f9d3e9787c8)

## Testing
- ✅ Validated API endpoint with various dice configurations
- ✅ Tested input validation for edge cases
- ✅ Verified all dice types work correctly
- ✅ Confirmed animations and UI responsiveness
- ✅ Security scan passed with no vulnerabilities (CodeQL)

## Files Added
- `server.js` - Express server with dice rolling logic
- `package.json` - Project dependencies and scripts
- `public/index.html` - Main web interface
- `public/style.css` - Styling and animations
- `public/app.js` - Client-side interaction logic
- `.gitignore` - Excludes node_modules and build artifacts
- Updated `README.md` with comprehensive usage instructions

Key Features:

Interactive Gameplay: The user can play multiple rounds against the computer.

Random Computer Choices: The computer's move ('s', 'w', or 'g') is selected randomly in each round using the random module.

Score Tracking: The script keeps track of wins for both the user and the computer.

Game Logic: Implements the classic rules of the game:

Snake drinks Water (Snake wins)

Gun shoots Snake (Gun wins)

Water rusts Gun (Water wins)

Clear User Interface: Provides simple and clear instructions for the user at each step, including the final score and the overall winner.

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

The system navigation bar was overlapping app elements (buttons, text, and interactive UI components) when the device was rotated to landscape orientation on Android. This made critical UI elements inaccessible to users, particularly on the Filters screen as shown in the issue screenshot.

**Device**: Motorola One Macro (Android 10)  
**Affected screens**: Primarily the Filters tab (third element in bottom navigation)

![Issue Screenshot](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d653c0e8-d07a-4ae1-9a06-19cd0ec564ee)

## Root Cause

The app was using `SafeAreaView` from `react-native`, which is primarily designed for iOS and doesn't properly handle Android system UI insets. This component doesn't account for:
- Android navigation bars (particularly in landscape mode)
- System gesture areas
- Different screen orientations and insets

## Solution

Replaced the iOS-focused `SafeAreaView` with the cross-platform implementation from `react-native-safe-area-context` (which was already a project dependency):

```javascript
// Before: iOS-focused, no Android inset handling
import { SafeAreaView } from 'react-native';
<SafeAreaView style={styles.container}>
  {children}
</SafeAreaView>

// After: Cross-platform with proper inset handling
import { SafeAreaView, SafeAreaProvider } from 'react-native-safe-area-context';
<SafeAreaProvider>
  <SafeAreaView style={styles.container} edges={['bottom', 'left', 'right']}>
    {children}
  </SafeAreaView>
</SafeAreaProvider>
```

### Key changes:
1. **Added `SafeAreaProvider`** - Wraps the app to provide safe area context to all child components
2. **Specified `edges={['bottom', 'left', 'right']}`** - Ensures proper padding is applied:
   - `bottom`: Prevents navigation bar from overlapping content
   - `left` & `right`: Adds appropriate spacing on sides in landscape mode
3. **Used proper Android inset API** - The library properly detects and responds to Android system UI

## Impact

✅ All app elements now remain fully visible and accessible in landscape mode  
✅ System navigation bar no longer overlaps interactive UI elements  
✅ Fix works across different Android devices and API levels  
✅ No breaking changes to existing functionality  
✅ Cross-platform solution works on both Android and iOS

## Testing Recommendations

1. Open the app and navigate to the Filters tab (third icon in bottom navigation)
2. Expand the first filter and select a city
3. Rotate device to landscape orientation
4. Verify that all UI elements (text, buttons, chips) are fully visible and not covered by the navigation bar
5. Test on devices with different navigation bar styles (3-button, 2-button, gesture navigation)

Fixes the issue reported where system UI overlapped app content in landscape mode.

## Problem

The previous PR intended to fix syntax errors in `algo/script.js` but was merged with 0 additions / 0 deletions, leaving the file with a critical syntax error that prevented the Algorithm Visualizer from loading. The page would show a persistent loading spinner and never initialize the UI.

The root cause was an **orphaned closing brace on line 2865** that didn't match any opening statement, causing:

```
/home/runner/work/WtMWs/WtMWs/algo/script.js:2865
}
^
SyntaxError: Unexpected token '}'
```

This prevented the entire JavaScript file from parsing, causing `initApp()` to never execute and the loading screen to never hide.

3. **Added a changelog comment** at the top of the file documenting the fix

### Code Structure

The `UIController` class has two main methods:
- `getAlgorithmInfo()` - returns algorithm metadata (closes at line 2727)
- `getAlgorithmCode()` - returns code examples (closes at line 2857)

The class properly closes at line 2858, but lines 2860-2865 incorrectly added:
```javascript
// UIController クラスの続き...
}
```

This extra closing brace had no matching opening statement, causing the syntax error.

author: dicxie1
body:
## Descripción

Este Pull Request introduce un nuevo endpoint para que las tiendas asociadas al marketplace puedan registrar nuevos productos. El endpoint recibe los datos del producto, incluyendo la ID de la tienda, realiza la validación necesaria y persiste la información en la base de datos.

Este es un paso crucial para habilitar la funcionalidad central del marketplace: la gestión de inventario por parte de los vendedores.

## Motivo

Se ha creado este endpoint para:
- Habilitar la gestión de inventario: Permitir que las tiendas publiquen sus productos de forma autónoma.
- Asegurar la trazabilidad: Garantizar que cada producto esté correctamente asociado a la ID de la tienda que lo registró.

## Cambios realizados

- Nuevo endpoint: Se agregó la ruta `POST /api/stores/product` para la creación de productos.
- Controlador: Se creó la función `setStoreProduct` en el registro de productos.
- Lógica: La lógica de negocio incluye la verificación de la existencia de la tienda (storeId) y la asignación automática de esa ID al nuevo producto antes de la inserción en la base de datos.

- **Prueba de éxito**: Se envió una solicitud POST al endpoint con datos de producto válidos y una storeId existente. Se verificó que el producto se creó correctamente y la respuesta fue `201 Created`.

body:
## Summary
Implements direct resource access to instruction modules via standardized `module://` URIs, enabling MCP clients to read module content in multiple formats without using tools.

## Features
- **URI scheme**: `module://{tier}/{category}/{subcategory}/{module-name}[/{format}]`
- **Three content formats**: markdown (default), yaml, raw
- **MIME type mapping** for proper content type handling
- **Comprehensive error handling** with helpful messages
- **Integration** with existing module parser cache

## Components Added
- `ResourceService`: URI parsing and module content retrieval
- `ResourceTypes`: Type definitions for resource functionality  
- `IResourceService` interface in dependency injection container
- `ReadResourceRequestSchema` handler in MCP server
- 28 comprehensive unit tests (all passing)

## Security Approach
This v1.0 implementation uses **basic security** relying on the existing `validateFilePath` function for path traversal protection.

### Security Features Deferred to v2.0
The following advanced security features are **explicitly deferred** to a future v2.0 release (documented in `docs/planning/docs-resources-implementation-plan.md`):

**For module:// URIs:**
- Six-layer defense-in-depth security model
- Custom `validateModulePath()` validation function
- Encoding attack prevention (percent-encoding rejection)
- Format suffix injection prevention
- Symlink detection and validation
- Cache integrity validation
- Whitelist enforcement beyond basic path checks
- 10+ additional security-focused tests

**Rationale for Deferral:**
- Get core functionality working quickly
- Monitor real-world usage patterns before hardening
- Existing `validateFilePath` provides baseline protection against path traversal
- Security enhancements can be added incrementally without breaking changes

**v2.0 Security Plan:**
A comprehensive security hardening plan is documented in `docs/planning/docs-resources-implementation-plan.md` covering both `module://` and future `docs://` resources with:
- OWASP Top 10 path traversal coverage
- Penetration testing requirements
- Security review checklist
- 35+ total security tests

## Testing
✅ All 28 tests passing  
✅ Integration tested with MCP client  
✅ Basic security validated (path traversal blocked)

## Complements
This resource capability complements existing tool-based discovery:
- `list_instruction_modules` - Browse available modules
- `search_instruction_modules` - Find modules by query
- `module://` URIs - Direct content access (new)

author: copilot
body:
## Overview

This PR implements an automated GitHub Actions workflow that generates and updates the changelog in README.md on every push to the main/master branch using **GitHub Copilot AI**. The workflow leverages GitHub's native Copilot service to analyze commits and generate meaningful, user-friendly changelog entries.

## Implementation

### Workflow Features

The workflow (`.github/workflows/update-changelog.yml`) provides:

- **Automatic triggering** on push events to main/master branches
- **AI-powered changelog generation** using GitHub Copilot that:
  - Analyzes commit messages, file changes, and diff statistics
  - Generates concise, user-friendly descriptions focused on what changed and why
  - Creates structured entries with 2-4 bullet points
  - Focuses on user/developer impact rather than implementation details
- **Fallback mechanism** for template-based generation when AI is unavailable
- **Smart information extraction** including:
  - Commit message and body
  - Author name
  - Commit date
  - Modified files
  - Diff statistics
- **README.md integration** that inserts new entries at the top of the Changelog section
- **Structured format** matching existing changelog style:
  ```markdown
  ### YYYY-MM-DD
  - **[AI-generated description]** (Author Name)
    - [Key change 1]
    - [Key change 2]
  ```

### AI Integration

- **Python Script**: Created `.github/workflows/generate_changelog_ai.py` that calls GitHub Copilot via GitHub Models API
- **Context-Aware**: Sends commit context including message, files, and diffs to GitHub Copilot
- **Intelligent Prompting**: Uses structured prompts to guide AI in generating user-friendly entries
- **Error Handling**: Gracefully falls back to template-based generation if API call fails
- **Native Integration**: Uses built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` for authentication - no external API keys required

**Configuration**: No additional setup required! The workflow uses the automatically available `GITHUB_TOKEN` to access GitHub Copilot through GitHub's Models API.

### Safety Mechanisms

To ensure reliable operation, the workflow includes:

1. **Infinite loop prevention**: Automatically skips commits containing "Update changelog" or "update-changelog" in the message
2. **Skip CI flag**: Uses `[skip ci]` in commit messages to prevent re-triggering
3. **Change detection**: Only commits when README.md is actually modified
4. **File filtering**: Excludes non-relevant files like workflow files, node_modules, and .git directories

### Documentation

- Added **"Automated Changelog"** section to README.md explaining the GitHub Copilot-powered workflow
- Created **`.github/workflows/README.md`** with comprehensive documentation including:
  - Detailed workflow explanation
  - GitHub Copilot integration guide
  - Permission requirements
  - Customization options
  - Troubleshooting guide
  - Example outputs (with and without AI)

## How to Use

Once merged, the workflow will automatically:
1. Detect every push to the main branch
2. Extract commit details and context
3. Call GitHub Copilot to generate intelligent changelog entry (or use fallback)
4. Update the README.md Changelog section
5. Commit and push the changes back

**No Setup Required**: The workflow uses the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` which is automatically available in all GitHub Actions workflows. GitHub Copilot generation is enabled by default.

No manual intervention is required - developers can continue their normal workflow and the changelog will be maintained automatically with AI-generated descriptions.

## Testing

- ✅ YAML syntax validated
- ✅ Changelog update logic tested with sample data
- ✅ Verified preservation of existing changelog entries
- ✅ Confirmed all safety features work correctly
- ✅ GitHub Copilot integration tested with proper error handling and fallback

The workflow will be fully tested on the first push after this PR is merged.

## Files Changed

- **`.github/workflows/update-changelog.yml`** (new): Main workflow file with GitHub Copilot integration
- **`.github/workflows/generate_changelog_ai.py`** (new): Python script for GitHub Copilot API calls
- **`.github/workflows/README.md`** (new): Comprehensive workflow and AI documentation
- **`README.md`** (modified): Added GitHub Copilot-powered changelog documentation section

body:
## Overview
This PR adds a sponsor popup that appears after users agree to the terms in the download flow, encouraging users to support the project while maintaining a seamless download experience. After confirming sponsorship, a thank you dialog appears before redirecting to the download.

## Changes

### User Flow
After users check all the required boxes and agree to the terms by clicking "GOGOGO", a new sponsor modal now appears asking **"是否愿意赞助?"** (Would you like to sponsor?) with the subtitle "您的支持是我们持续开发的动力".

Users are presented with two choices:
- **确认 (Confirm)**: Opens the sponsor page (https://afdian.com/a/dwhlqwq), then shows a thank you dialog. Users must click "跳转到网盘" to proceed to the download link.
- **取消 (Cancel)**: Opens only the download link

**New Thank You Dialog**: After clicking "确认", a thank you dialog appears with:
- Title: "感谢您的赞助" (Thank you for your sponsorship)
- Subtitle: "点击跳转到网盘" (Click to jump to cloud storage)
- Button: "跳转到网盘" to open the download link

This approach is non-intrusive as users can skip sponsorship while still getting access to their download.

### Technical Implementation

**Modified file**: `download/comp.vue` (+295 lines, -2 lines)

#### JavaScript Changes
1. Added `showSponsorModal` ref to control the sponsor modal's visibility
2. Added `showThankYouModal` ref to control the thank you dialog's visibility
3. Modified `check_question()` to close the terms modal and show the sponsor modal instead of directly opening the download link
4. Added `handleSponsorConfirm()` handler to open sponsor page and show thank you dialog
5. Added `handleSponsorCancel()` handler to open only the download link when user cancels
6. Added `handleThankYouClick()` handler to open the download link from the thank you dialog

#### Template Changes
Added two new modal components using Naive UI's `n-modal`:

**Sponsor Modal:**
- Centered card layout with glass-morphism effect
- Pulsing heart emoji icon (💝)
- Clear title and subtitle text
- Two styled action buttons with distinct visual hierarchy

**Thank You Modal:**
- Centered card with celebration emoji icon (🎉)
- Green gradient title for success theme
- "跳转到网盘" button to proceed to download
- Bounce animation for celebration effect

#### CSS Styles
- Complete styling with modern gradient design for both modals
- Pink/rose gradient for the sponsor confirm button
- Gray styling for the cancel button
- Green gradient for thank you title
- Pulse animation (2s loop) for the heart icon
- Bounce animation (1s) for the celebration icon
- Smooth hover effects with lift and shadow
- Full dark mode support with appropriate color adjustments
- Responsive design that works on mobile devices (90vw width)

## Design Highlights

Both modals follow the existing design system with:
- Backdrop blur effect matching other modals
- Purple/green gradient accents consistent with the site theme
- Smooth transitions and animations
- Proper spacing and typography
- Accessible button sizes (48px height) for easy clicking

## Screenshots
The sponsor modal appears as a centered card with:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│              💝 (pulsing)           │
│                                     │
│         是否愿意赞助?                │
│   您的支持是我们持续开发的动力        │
│                                     │
│   [❤️ 确认]      [⏭️ 取消]         │
└─────────────────────────────────────┘
```

After clicking "确认", the thank you dialog appears:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│              🎉 (bouncing)          │
│                                     │
│         感谢您的赞助                 │
│        点击跳转到网盘                │
│                                     │
│     [📦 跳转到网盘]                 │
└─────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Testing Recommendations
- Verify both "确认" and "取消" buttons work correctly
- Verify thank you dialog appears after clicking "确认"
- Verify download link opens when clicking "跳转到网盘"
- Test the responsive design on mobile devices
- Check dark mode appearance for both modals
- Ensure animations are smooth
- Verify no breaking changes to existing download flow

## Notes
This implementation maintains backward compatibility and does not block users from downloading if they choose not to sponsor. All users can access downloads regardless of their choice, making this a user-friendly way to encourage support while providing clear acknowledgment of sponsorship actions.

body:
This pull request enhances how old datasets are handled and curated by introducing robust mapping and enrichment of resource types and licenses from the legacy database to the ERNIE system. It improves both backend data enrichment and frontend mapping logic, and updates tests to reflect these changes.

**Backend data enrichment:**

* Each dataset returned by `OldDatasetController` now includes a `licenses` property, populated by querying the license table for each resource. This ensures licenses are available for downstream processing and UI display. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ce563f3724dd5a3e00838a6b6dca29f0bedfabff1db9a32a3b06d91d3dff1c49R36-R43) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ce563f3724dd5a3e00838a6b6dca29f0bedfabff1db9a32a3b06d91d3dff1c49R96-R103) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-8c93c3df47ab824fe7841f40c203c0e7fa795151cba9461161edfbf0ab43f7faR10-R12) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-8c93c3df47ab824fe7841f40c203c0e7fa795151cba9461161edfbf0ab43f7faR121-R144)

**Frontend mapping and API integration:**

* Added async functions `getResourceTypes` and `getLicenses` to fetch and cache ERNIE resource types and licenses, minimizing repeated API calls. These are preloaded on page mount for efficiency. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-19ec52e4ebf5106e3f9d15745396d8d0adab8297d90304f47864cac3b5510b2eL345-R499) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-19ec52e4ebf5106e3f9d15745396d8d0adab8297d90304f47864cac3b5510b2eR623-R628)
* Implemented robust mapping functions (`mapResourceTypeToId`, `mapLicenseToIdentifier`) to convert legacy resource type strings and license names into ERNIE-compatible identifiers for curation queries.
* Refactored `buildCurationQuery` to use the new mapping logic, ensuring resource type and license fields are correctly mapped for curation routing. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-19ec52e4ebf5106e3f9d15745396d8d0adab8297d90304f47864cac3b5510b2eL364-R523) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-19ec52e4ebf5106e3f9d15745396d8d0adab8297d90304f47864cac3b5510b2eR532-R541) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-19ec52e4ebf5106e3f9d15745396d8d0adab8297d90304f47864cac3b5510b2eL423-R589)

**Testing improvements:**

* Updated feature tests to expect datasets with the new `licenses` property, ensuring test coverage for enriched dataset payloads. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0a43e9d11c6fb3959ba10fae91cfe32063ed1c2f820c278c2b48b8363865e4d0L28-R29) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0a43e9d11c6fb3959ba10fae91cfe32063ed1c2f820c278c2b48b8363865e4d0L40-R43) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-0a43e9d11c6fb3959ba10fae91cfe32063ed1c2f820c278c2b48b8363865e4d0L52-R57) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-0a43e9d11c6fb3959ba10fae91cfe32063ed1c2f820c278c2b48b8363865e4d0R73-R107) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-0a43e9d11c6fb3959ba10fae91cfe32063ed1c2f820c278c2b48b8363865e4d0L121-R155) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-0a43e9d11c6fb3959ba10fae91cfe32063ed1c2f820c278c2b48b8363865e4d0L133-R169) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-0a43e9d11c6fb3959ba10fae91cfe32063ed1c2f820c278c2b48b8363865e4d0R185-R205)
* Enhanced frontend tests to mock fetch calls for resource types and licenses, and validated correct mapping of resource type IDs in curation queries. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3ed989a2c15604b277d16ddf5abfab8d6a732b7042581cd5b8fa7ac207be11f4R126-R150) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3ed989a2c15604b277d16ddf5abfab8d6a732b7042581cd5b8fa7ac207be11f4R281-R291) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-3ed989a2c15604b277d16ddf5abfab8d6a732b7042581cd5b8fa7ac207be11f4L291-R319)

These changes ensure that old datasets are correctly enriched and mapped to ERNIE standards, improving both backend data quality and frontend curation workflows.

body:
## Description
This PR adds support for signed int with REST API and transaction arguments. It does the following
1. Add `FatType` for signed ints, and add convertions `MoveTypeLayout <-> FatType` and `TypeTag -> FatType`
2. Add `AnnotatedMoveValue` for signed int together with desired serialization, and add convertions  `(MoreCore MoveValue, FatType) -> AnnotatedMoveValue` 
3. Add `TransactionArgument` for signed int, and add convertions  `TransactionArgument <-> MoreCore MoveValue` 
4. Add `REST API MoveType` for signed int, and add convertions `TypeTag <-> REST API MoveType`
5. Add `REST API MoveValue` (Rust primitive type representation for `i8`, `i16`, and `i32`, and string represetation for `i64`, `i128`, and `i256`) for singed int together with desired serialization, and add convertions `TransactionArgument -> REST API MoveValue` and `AnnotatedMoveValue -> REST API MoveValue`
6. Add Poem OpenAPI types for signed int.

Example Input Flow:
`serde_json Value` (from client) -> `MoreCore MoveValue` -> `TransactionArgument` -> `Vec<u8>` -> `MoveVM Value` (to MoveVM).

Example Output Flow: 
`MoveVM value` (from MoveVM) -> `(Vec<u8>, MoveTypeLayout)` -> `MoveCore MoveValue` -> `AnnotatedMoveValue` -> `REST API MoveValue` -> JSON (to client)

body:
Our previous kernels took in scales directly, but we store log(scales) to ensure the parameter is always valid. This change makes the projection kernel accept logScales instead, avoiding an extra operation (and derivative). 

This change requires us to update the gtests to use higher tolerances since the original test data was computed using scales as input rather than logScales. While the tolerances are larger, they are still a tiny fraction of the actual range of the data, so probably fine. 

I've also trained several splats in reality capture with this change. The only difference is a slight speedup.

Thanks @matthewdcong for the original code (I just fixed up the tests).

Description

This pull request adds a new keypad combinations problem (classic T9 text prediction style) along with its solution. The problem statement describes generating all possible words from a sequence of digits entered on a mobile keypad, where each digit maps to specific characters (2 → "abc", 3 → "def", etc.). The solution is implemented using recursion and backtracking to explore all possible letter combinations.

Fixes: #<issue_number>

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

The mobile menu was appearing at the same z-index level as the GraphicHero heading text, causing visual layering issues on mobile devices. Both elements had `z-index: 10`, which meant that when the mobile menu was open, the GraphicHero text could appear on top of or at the same level as the menu, creating a confusing user experience.

Additionally, the mobile menu lacked a solid background color, which could cause contrast issues depending on what content was behind it.

## Solution

This PR fixes the z-index hierarchy and improves accessibility:

1. **Increased mobile menu z-index from 10 to 40** - This ensures the mobile menu appears above all page content while remaining below the menu toggle button (z-index: 50)

2. **Added semi-transparent background color** - Added `background-color: rgba(255, 254, 252, 0.95)` to provide consistent, high-contrast background for menu items

## Changes

Modified `src/components/layout/nav/Navbar.astro`:
- Changed `#menu-main-group` z-index from `10` to `40`
- Added `background-color: rgba(255, 254, 252, 0.95)` to `#menu-main-group`

## Z-index Hierarchy

After this fix, the layering order is now correct:
- InPageNav: 1000
- Menu toggle button: 50
- **Mobile menu: 40** ✅ (fixed)
- Page content (GraphicHero, etc.): 10 or below

## Visual Verification

**Mobile view with menu closed:**

![Mobile view before opening menu](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0e5a2730-cf89-47d7-9686-614aff68c511)

**Mobile menu open - now properly overlays all content:**

![Mobile menu open with fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5d0cb0f1-88d0-4fc4-a274-0673ad3b85f5)

The mobile menu now correctly overlays the GraphicHero heading and all other page content, with excellent color contrast ensuring all menu items are easily readable.

## Testing

Tested on `/submissions` page at mobile viewport (375x667px) to verify:
- ✅ Mobile menu appears above GraphicHero heading text
- ✅ Menu items have sufficient color contrast
- ✅ Menu toggle button remains clickable
- ✅ Build completes successfully

Fixes issue with z-index layering reported in the original bug report.

body:
## Which issue does this PR close?
- Closes #76 

## Rationale for this change
The cab sharing page had critical UI/UX issues that negatively impacted user experience:
- Mobile version was causing horizontal scrolling issues (cursor moving content sideways)
- Header elements (Toggle Mode and Home buttons) were overlapping/merging in laptop view
- Outdated design that didn't align with modern web standards
- Missing essential features for a complete cab sharing experience

## What changes are included in this PR?

### Bug Fixes:
- Fixed horizontal scrolling issue on mobile devices by adding `overflow-x: hidden` and proper box-sizing
- Redesigned header layout with flexible wrapping to prevent button overlap
- Fixed map rendering issues with `map.invalidateSize()`
- Corrected responsive breakpoints for better mobile experience

### New Features:
- **Date & Time Picker**: Users can now select travel date and time
- **Vehicle Type Selection**: Choose between Sedan (₹12/km), SUV (₹18/km), or Mini (₹10/km)
- **Detailed Fare Breakdown**: Shows distance, rate per km, passengers, total fare, and per-person cost
- **Statistics Dashboard**: Three animated cards displaying Total Fare, Per Person Cost, and Distance
- **Feature Badges**: Highlights key features (AC Vehicle, Comfortable Seats, Live Tracking, Safe & Secure)
- **Enhanced Map Visualization**: Color-coded markers (Green=Start, Red=End, Yellow=Via) with improved route display

### UI/UX Improvements:
- Modern gradient design with glassmorphism effects
- Smooth animations and hover effects on all interactive elements
- Improved dark mode with better contrast and theming
- Better form labels and field organization
- Responsive design optimized for all screen sizes
- Added descriptive tagline: "Share Your Ride, Split Your Fare!"

## Are these changes tested?

Yes, these changes have been tested:
- ✅ Mobile responsiveness tested on various screen sizes (320px to 1920px)
- ✅ Dark mode toggle functionality verified
- ✅ Form validation tested with various input combinations
- ✅ Map rendering tested across different routes and scenarios
- ✅ Fare calculation accuracy verified for all vehicle types
- ✅ Cross-browser compatibility (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge)
- ✅ Touch interactions tested on mobile devices

## Are there any user-facing changes?

Yes, significant user-facing changes:
- **Complete UI redesign** with modern gradient aesthetics
- **New interactive elements**: date picker, time picker, vehicle selector
- **Enhanced information display**: fare breakdown and statistics cards
- **Improved navigation**: fixed header layout with proper spacing
- **Better mobile experience**: no horizontal scrolling, optimized touch targets
- **Dark mode enhancement**: smoother transitions and better color schemes

body:
## Overview

This PR provides comprehensive documentation for consolidating EasyCart's backend deployments on Render.com, ensuring only one production service (`easycart-backend-0u8r`) remains active and properly configured. This addresses the issue of multiple backend services causing confusion and maintenance overhead.

## Problem

Multiple backend services have been deployed on Render:
- `easycart-backend-0u8r` (primary production)
- `easycart-j6ue` (secondary/legacy)
- `easycart-backend-d3b90j3e5dus73cc8bjg` (mentioned in docs)

This multiplicity created:
- Configuration inconsistencies between services
- Confusion about which backend is production
- Duplication of environment variables
- Increased maintenance burden
- Potential for requests hitting the wrong backend

## Solution

This PR provides complete documentation to consolidate all backend deployments into a single production service: **easycart-backend-0u8r** (`https://easycart-backend-0u8r.onrender.com/`)

## Description

Implements node-level timeouts to prevent nodes from getting stuck in QUEUED status indefinitely.

Fixes #444

## Changes

### Core Implementation
- **New Status**: Added `TIMEDOUT` status to `StateStatusEnum` for timed-out nodes
- **Database**: Added `queued_at` timestamp field to `State` model with optimized index for timeout queries
- **Configuration**: Added `NODE_TIMEOUT_MINUTES` environment variable (default: 30 minutes)
- **Scheduled Task**: Created `check_node_timeout` task that runs every minute to detect and timeout stuck nodes
- **Enqueue Logic**: Updated state enqueuing to record `queued_at` timestamp

### Testing
- Added comprehensive unit tests covering timeout detection, threshold calculation, and error handling
- All existing tests pass without regression

## How It Works

1. When a state transitions to QUEUED, the system records the current timestamp in `queued_at`
2. Every minute, a background task scans for QUEUED states older than the configured timeout
3. Timed-out states are automatically marked as TIMEDOUT with a descriptive error message
4. The timeout duration is configurable via `NODE_TIMEOUT_MINUTES` environment variable

author: copilot
body:
This PR adds Azure DevOps pipeline support to the templates, allowing users to choose between GitHub Actions and Azure DevOps Pipelines when creating a new project.

## Changes

### New Pipeline Parameter

All templates now include a `--pipeline` parameter that accepts two values:
- `github` (default) - Generates project with `.github` folder containing GitHub Actions workflows
- `azuredevops` - Generates project with `.devops` folder containing Azure DevOps YAML pipelines

Example usage:
```bash
# Default - uses GitHub Actions
dotnet new keboo.wpf --name MyApp

# Use Azure DevOps Pipelines
dotnet new keboo.wpf --name MyApp --pipeline azuredevops

# Short form also available
dotnet new keboo.wpf --name MyApp -p azuredevops
```

### Azure DevOps Pipelines

Created `.devops` folders alongside existing `.github` folders for:
- **WPF Template**: Multi-stage pipeline with build, test, code coverage, and artifact publishing
- **Console Template**: Build, test, and code coverage reporting
- **NuGet Library Template**: Build, test, pack, and deploy to NuGet.org with multi-stage pipeline

All Azure DevOps pipelines include:
- Trigger configuration for main branch and pull requests
- .NET 8.x SDK setup
- Build and test steps with code coverage collection
- Native Azure DevOps code coverage reporting using ReportGenerator
- Artifact publishing for deployments
- Proper multi-stage structure for CI/CD workflows

### Conditional Exclusion

Template configuration now ensures only one CI/CD folder is included based on the parameter:
- When `--pipeline github` (default): `.github` folder included, `.devops` excluded
- When `--pipeline azuredevops`: `.devops` folder included, `.github` excluded

This keeps generated projects clean with only the relevant CI/CD configuration.

### Documentation

Updated README files for:
- Main repository README with information about the new parameter
- WPF, Console, and NuGet template READMEs with usage examples and parameter documentation

### Compatibility

- **Backward Compatible**: Default behavior unchanged - GitHub Actions remains the default
- **Works with Existing Parameters**: Correctly integrates with `--no-tests`, `--no-sln`, etc.
- **Conditional Compilation**: Azure DevOps pipelines respect template conditionals (e.g., test steps excluded when `--no-tests` is used)

## Testing

Verified functionality across all three templates:
- ✅ Default GitHub option generates `.github` folder only
- ✅ Azure DevOps option generates `.devops` folder only  
- ✅ Help text displays parameter correctly
- ✅ Conditional compilation works with `--no-tests` flag
- ✅ Generated pipelines have valid YAML syntax

Fixes Keboo/DotnetTemplates#100

body:
Closes #99

## Overview

This PR adds `global.json` files to the repository and all templates to ensure users have the required .NET SDK version. The GitHub Actions workflows have been updated to use these files, and documentation has been added explaining how to update .NET versions.

## Changes

### global.json Files
Added `global.json` to:
- Repository root (specifies .NET SDK 9.0.100)
- WPF template
- Console template  
- NuGet Library template
- Avalonia template

All files use `"rollForward": "latestFeature"` to allow flexibility with newer SDK versions while ensuring minimum requirements are met.

### GitHub Actions Workflows
Updated workflows to use the `global-json-file` parameter:

- **Root workflow** (`.github/workflows/build.yml`): Build job now uses `global-json-file: global.json`. Test jobs continue to use the environment variable for SDK version installation.
- **Template workflows**: WPF, Console, and NuGet template workflows now reference their respective global.json files using the `global-json-file` parameter.

### Documentation
Added "Updating .NET Version" sections to template README files:

- **Template READMEs**: Each template README now includes concise instructions for updating the .NET SDK version, specifying to update both the `global.json` file and the `<TargetFramework>` in csproj files.

## Benefits

1. **Consistency**: Developers using the templates will have the correct .NET SDK installed automatically
2. **CI/CD Reliability**: Pipelines will use the SDK version specified in global.json, reducing version-related failures
3. **Maintainability**: Updating .NET versions is now centralized in global.json files with clear documentation
4. **Transparency**: Users can easily see which .NET version is required by inspecting global.json

## Testing

All templates have been tested:
- ✅ Template package builds successfully
- ✅ Console app template creates projects with global.json and builds/tests successfully
- ✅ NuGet library template creates projects with global.json and builds/tests successfully
- ✅ WPF and Avalonia templates verified to include global.json and updated workflows
- ✅ All workflows properly reference global.json files

body:
Ensures onError sequences are resolved correctly by removing duplicate/invalid mediator execution paths. This prevents unexpected behavior when mediation is aborted and an error handler is invoked.

Adds callback-controlled acknowledgement for RabbitMQ inbound listener. A latch-based callback mechanism is introduced, allowing mediation to explicitly decide between ACKNOWLEDGE, SET_ROLLBACK_ONLY, or REQUEUE. This prevents premature acks and enables safe retries.

body:
## Amazon Prime Video Clone – CI/CD Pipeline

This PR introduces a complete CI/CD pipeline for deploying the Amazon Prime Video Clone application, integrating code quality checks, security scans, containerization, and monitoring.

### Tech Stack & Tools

* **CI/CD**: Jenkins
* **Code Quality**: SonarQube (static analysis, quality gates)
* **Security**: Trivy (vulnerability scanning)
* **Containerization**: Docker
* **Registry**: AWS Elastic Container Registry (ECR)
* **Deployment**: ArgoCD on **Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)**
* **Monitoring**: Prometheus & Grafana
* **Languages/Frameworks**: Node.js, npm
* **Infrastructure**: AWS EC2 (Jenkins, SonarQube), AKS cluster, AWS CLI

### Pipeline Flow

1. Checkout source code from GitHub.
2. Run SonarQube analysis and validate quality gates.
3. Install npm dependencies.
4. Perform Trivy vulnerability scan.
5. Build and tag Docker image.
6. Push image to AWS ECR (auto-creates repo if needed).
7. Deploy with ArgoCD to AKS.
8. Monitor workloads with Prometheus and Grafana.
9. Clean up unused Docker images from Jenkins server.

### Outcome

Delivers a **secure, automated, and scalable CI/CD pipeline** that ensures:

* Enforced code quality and security checks.
* Reliable containerized deployments via ArgoCD on AKS.
* Centralized monitoring with Prometheus and Grafana.

body:
## Summary
Replace `time.Tick` with `time.NewTicker` in the OpenTSDB exporter to enable explicit stop and prevent leaked timers.

## Rationale
`time.Tick` cannot be stopped and may leak timers/goroutines over time. `time.NewTicker` allows proper lifecycle management and graceful shutdown.

## Changes

body: Technically, to be 100% compatible, this should be calling through a metatable assigned to all strings which has __index pointing to the string global table. (It is not possible to *set* a metatable on a string in PUC-Lua, but it is at least possible to call `getmetatable` on a string and then mess with it.)

This PR introduces a game-changing referral rewards system that turns satisfied users into active promoters, creating exponential growth opportunities for the platform.

## What's New
- **Referral Code Generation**: Users create unique codes to share with their network

Traditional marketing is expensive and impersonal. This feature leverages the most powerful marketing channel: word-of-mouth from trusted sources. When users earn rewards for sharing datasets they genuinely value, everyone wins.

- Zero breaking changes to existing functionality

- Efficient map-based tracking with minimal storage overhead
- Seamless integration with current purchase flow

- **Lower CAC**: Community-driven acquisition costs fraction of traditional marketing
- **Higher Quality Users**: Referred users come pre-validated by trusted sources
- **Increased Engagement**: Financial incentives drive active participation
- **Network Effects**: Each new user becomes potential growth channel

body:
This pull request introduces the GeeksforGeeks Problem of the Day for October 3, 2025, "Possible Words From Phone Digits," with a comprehensive PowerShell implementation, documentation, and testing. The most important changes include the addition of a detailed problem description and constraints, a robust and well-documented PowerShell solution, and extensive test and benchmark coverage to ensure correctness and performance.

### Problem documentation and explanation
* Added a detailed `README.md` with problem statement, examples, constraints, solution approach, complexity analysis, usage instructions, test results, performance benchmarks, and related problems for "Possible Words From Phone Digits."

### PowerShell implementation
* Implemented the `Get-PossibleWords` function in `possible_words_from_phone_digits.ps1`, which generates all valid word combinations from a sequence of phone digits using an iterative approach, including input validation and sorted output.

### Testing and benchmarking
* Added `Test-PossibleWords` and `Benchmark-PossibleWords` functions to the script, providing automated test coverage for edge cases and performance measurement for various input sizes.

### Usage and documentation
* Included usage instructions, example calls, and inline documentation for the PowerShell functions, making the solution easy to run and understand. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-287c823fa9610aa76179ab94e06fb5b37bc6af3dc17b8b7aebe7b38137c3241bR1-R197) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-5f921a659807dda7396aa1673432bd9a749e4d412a3d77610f456f21b98a37afR1-R201)

### Edge case handling and robustness
* Ensured the implementation gracefully handles empty input, invalid digits (0, 1), and provides sorted output, with all test cases passing.Add complete solution for "Possible Words From Phone Digits" problem with PowerShell implementation, comprehensive testing, and performance benchmarks. Includes iterative approach to generate all possible letter combinations from phone keypad digit sequences.

author: guillaq
body:
Implements PostHog analytics integration as a structlog processor as requested in #376.

### Changes
- Create PostHogProcessor that sends events when `analytics=<event_name>` is in log context
- Build event properties from structlog context (excluding internal keys)
- Configure with `POSTHOG_API_KEY` and `POSTHOG_HOST` environment variables
- Integrate processor into setup_logs.py pipeline
- Add posthog>=3.7.2 dependency to pyproject.toml

### Usage
To track analytics events, add `analytics=<event_name>` to log context:
```python
log.info("User signed up", analytics="user_signup", user_id="123")
```

Closes #376

author: paultranvan
body:
The app mouting the Provider can provide options. If no option is provided, a default `{}` is given.
The reference of this `{}` will change everytime, so if we pass it in dependency array on a `useEffect`, it will be trigger everytime, making an infinite loop.
This typically happened with Home, that does give any option, but not in Drive, that provide options.

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

The RPM packaging build in the GitHub Actions workflow was failing with the following error:

```
RPM: error: /github/home/rpmbuild/SPECS/caso.spec: line 8: Too many levels of recursion in macro expansion.
It is likely caused by recursive macro declaration.
```

This error occurred when building RPM packages for releases with version strings containing "dev" (e.g., `5.1.1.dev1`), preventing the packaging workflow from completing successfully.

## Root Cause

The `packaging/redhat/caso.spec` file had a circular macro definition on line 2:

```spec
Version:     %{version}
```

When RPM parses the spec file, it automatically creates a `%{version}` macro from the value in the `Version:` tag. Since the tag itself was set to `%{version}`, this created infinite recursion when RPM tried to expand the macro.

## Solution

Added a conditional default version definition at the top of the spec file:

```spec
%{!?version:%define version 5.1.0}
```

This RPM macro expression means: "if the `version` macro is not already defined, define it as 5.1.0". This approach:

- Provides a sensible default version when building manually
- Allows the rpmbuild GitHub action to override it with `--define "version X.Y.Z"` 
- Breaks the circular reference that was preventing builds
- Follows standard RPM spec file practices for templated versions

## Testing

Validated the fix locally using `rpm --define "version X.Y.Z" -q --specfile` with multiple version formats:

- ✅ `5.1.0` - standard release
- ✅ `5.1.1` - standard release  
- ✅ `5.1.1.dev1` - development version (previously failing)
- ✅ `5.1.1.rc1` - release candidate
- ✅ `5.1.1.post1` - post-release

All versions now parse correctly without recursion errors.

## Changes

- Modified `packaging/redhat/caso.spec` (1 line added)
- No changes to DEB packaging (was already working)
- Minimal, surgical fix that only affects RPM build process

Fixes the RPM build failures reported in the packaging workflow.

body: Ignore forwarded, photo, and document messages when the user is in settings input mode to prevent incorrect processing. Previously, the `handle_forwarded_message` (and similarly `handle_photo_message`, `handle_document_message`) did not check if the user was `waiting_for_input`. author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
This commit fixes a bug where some facial expressions on the VRM avatar would snap instantly instead of animating smoothly.

The `useFrame` hook in `VRMAvatar.tsx` was only applying smooth interpolation (lerp) to a subset of facial expressions. This commit refactors the hook to apply the `lerpExpression` function to all expressions, including `angry`, `sad`, and `happy`, ensuring a consistent and polished animation for all facial controls.

This change addresses the issue by unifying the expression update logic into a single loop, making the code cleaner and the animations smoother.

author: katspaugh
body:
## Description

This PR fixes multiple type safety issues and improves error handling across the codebase.

## Implementation Details

### Bugs Fixed

1. **TypeScript Type Error in decoder.ts**
   - Fixed type incompatibility with `getChannelData` return type
   - Added proper Float32Array conversion for consistency
   - Improved error handling for missing channels

2. **Stack Overflow Risk in fetcher.ts**
   - Replaced recursive `read()` function with iterative while loop
   - Prevents potential stack overflow with large files
   - Added better error logging

3. **Missing Error Emission in wavesurfer.ts**
   - Constructor now properly emits error events when initial load fails
   - Improved debugging experience for users

4. **Unhandled Errors in webaudio.ts**
   - Added catch block to handle fetch failures
   - Prevents silent errors in WebAudio loading

5. **Variable Shadowing in wavesurfer.ts**
   - Fixed loop variable shadowing in `exportPeaks()` method
   - Renamed inner loop variable from `i` to `j`

6. **Null Safety Issue in wavesurfer.ts**
   - Fixed TypeScript strictness issue with dragToSeek handling
   - Added proper type narrowing and assertions

## How to Test It

```bash
# Run linter
yarn lint

# Run unit tests
yarn test:unit

# Verify TypeScript compilation
npx tsc --noEmit src/*.ts
```

## Checklist

- [x] Code follows the repo's style guidelines
- [x] Self-review completed
- [x] Changes generate no new warnings
- [x] Added tests for new code (N/A - bug fixes)
- [x] All new and existing tests pass
- [x] Linting passes
- [x] Changes are backward compatible

## Validation Results

✅ **81/81 unit tests passing**  
✅ **ESLint validation clean**  
✅ **TypeScript compilation successful**

## Impact

- Improves type safety across the codebase
- Prevents potential runtime errors with large files
- Makes debugging easier with proper error emission
- No breaking changes - fully backward compatible

author: mbwilding
body:
So I made modifications to the rust toolchain.

1. Unsafe checks removed
2. Variables are mutable by default (`let` rather than `let mut`)
3. Mutable pointers by default (Can use pointers like `*` instead of `*mut` or `**` rather than `*mut *mut`)

Just a proof of concept of what Crust could be with a bit of effort.
Would be cool to see azozin implement the pub by default stuff.

Raised this PR mainly to spark something in people. Don't expect it to get merged as it would require a custom pipeline to apply patches to rust and publish releases.

The Crust version of the Rust toolchain is here: https://github.com/mbwilding/rust

author: alexdewar
body:
# Description

As part of the series of fixes for reduced costs (#876), we will soon be transitioning to using the same method for calculating reduced costs as we currently do for existing costs (#879). This means that candidate assets will need to be associated with a particular agent, as the reduced cost calculation will vary depending on the agent's objective (see my other PR: #882). Currently, candidate assets are agent-less unless and until they are selected by an agent, at which point their `state` is changed to `AssetState::Selected` and they are assigned an agent ID. All other asset types already have an associated agent ID; this PR just changes things so candidates have one too, by making `agent_id` a field of `Asset` rather than a value embedded in different `AssetState` variants.

This means we have to use a different method for generating candidate assets for a given year: now we iterate over agents and look at their search spaces, so we have a corresponding agent for each, rather than just looking at the set of processes which can be commissioned in a given year instead.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change to fix an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change to add functionality)
- [x] Refactoring (non-breaking, non-functional change to improve maintainability)
- [ ] Optimization (non-breaking change to speed up the code)
- [ ] Breaking change (whatever its nature)
- [ ] Documentation (improve or add documentation)

## Key checklist

- [ ] All tests pass: `$ cargo test`
- [ ] The documentation builds and looks OK: `$ cargo doc`

## Further checks

- [ ] Code is commented, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] Tests added that prove fix is effective or that feature works

author: shubham220420
body:
## PR Description

**Summary:**  
Add Python solution for 407 “Trapping Rain Water II” and update README.

**Changes:**  
- Created `Trapping_rain_water_II.py` file  
- Updated `README.md` with approach

**Approach:**  
We start from the **boundary cells (walls)** and use a **min-heap** to always process the **lowest wall first**. For each cell, we check its neighbors: if a neighbor is lower, water is trapped equal to `boundary_height - neighbor_height`, then we push the neighbor with height = `max(neighbor_height, boundary_height)`. Repeat until all cells are visited.

**Complexity:**  
- **Time:** O(m * n * log(m * n))  
- **Space:** O(m * n)

author: ibinola
body:
This PR adds a new set of endpoints to the `API` for creating, reading, and updating Root Cause Analysis (RCA) entries. This functionality is essential for our incident management process, allowing teams to document post-mortems for outage reports.

**Key Changes:**
- Pydantic Model (RcaModel): A new RcaModel has been defined to ensure that all RCA entries are structured correctly, with validated fields for the incident timeline, root cause analysis, and corrective actions.
- CRUD Operations: The following endpoints have been implemented:
- Create (`POST /rca/{ticket_id}`): Allows for the submission of a new RCA document tied to a specific outage ticket ID.
- Read (`GET /rca/{ticket_id}`): Retrieves the details of an existing RCA.
- Update (`PUT /rca/{ticket_id}`): Allows for the modification of an RCA after it has been created.

Closes #15

author: itzikvaknin
body:
`parseHybridCommand` creates upstream `areqs` as a standalone component, but these are not needed in the coordinator.  

Instead, the coordinator follows a two-pipeline structure:
```RPDepleter -> RPSorter ->RPNet``` 

(as detailed in the [Hybrid Search RRF and Linear Combination Design Doc](https://redislabs.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DX/pages/5164236959/Hybrid+Search+RRF+and+Linear+Combination+-+Design+Doc)).

As part of this change, the previous `areqs` are removed and replaced with new ones built according to this model.


#### Sorter Logic
Heap size is determined as follows:

```
search: window
vsim: min(window, knn_k)
```

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> Introduce coordinator subqueries in hybrid: rebuild upstream requests, set sorter heap to window/min(window,K), and wire score-sorting; adjust flags to include coordinator and shift NO_SORT bit.
> 
> - **Hybrid coordinator execution**:
>   - Rebuild upstream `AREQ`s via `hybridRequestSetupCoordinatorSubqueriesRequests()`; mark both as `QEXEC_F_IS_HYBRID_COORDINATOR_SUBQUERY` and set `PLN_ArrangeStep->limit` to `window` (search) and `min(window, K)` (KNN vector).
>   - Use the new setup in `HybridRequest_prepareForExecution()` and build depletion/merge pipelines accordingly.
>   - Ensure upstreams use score sorting by extending sorter condition to include `IsHybridCoordinatorSubquery()`.
> - **Flags and helpers**:
>   - Add `QEXEC_F_IS_HYBRID_COORDINATOR_SUBQUERY` and `IsHybridCoordinatorSubquery()`; include in `IsHybrid()`.
>   - Shift `QEXEC_F_NO_SORT` bit to avoid overlap.
>

## Motivation

Fix some bugs related to RockPipeline pass. This will be needed for attention pipelining (outer loop).

## Technical Details

- RockMultibuffer.h: Make cpp and .h name of variables match
- GridwiseGemmToBlockwise.cpp: Use different registers for input and output (postProcessFirstGemmSplat), otherwise multibuffering had some issues.
- RockMultibuffer.cpp: Remove limitation of not multibuffering non-i8 + one dimensions buffers. This was to only let LDS buffers get multibuffered (I guess), because we define LDS buffers in this particular way.
- RockPipeline.cpp: Fix bug due to uninitialized thisMultiBuffers[key], if the key doesn't exist, it's init to 0, instead of 1. Also added some checks to make the pass fail.
- loweringUtils.cpp: Fix bug when handling rock.extract_multibuffer, it must do modulo of the index.
